newsitem.title: USA: "First Wives" fends off box office rivals.
newsitem.headline: "First Wives" fends off box office rivals.

text.p: "The First Wives Club" withstood the arrival of three potent new releases to lead the box office for the third weekend in a row, according to studio estimates released Sunday.
The comedic tale of three vengeful ex-wives earned an estimated $11.1 million during the Friday to Sunday period, taking its three-week total to $58.65 million.
The movie stars Bette Midler, Diane Keaton and Goldie Hawn and is released by Paramount Pictures, a unit of Viacom Inc.
As a testament to its staying power, the film earned $4,801 per screen, the highest average in the top 10.

"The Glimmer Man", an action thriller starring Steven Seagal and Keenen Ivory Wayans, opened in second with $7.6 million and a decent average of $3,399. The movie is released by Time Warner Inc's Warner Bros.

Third and fourth was a tight race between "That Thing You Do!", the highly praised directorial debut of Tom Hanks, and "D3: The Mighty Ducks", the third instalment of Walt Disney Co's ice hockey franchise.

The Hanks movie, which is released by News Corp's 20th Century Fox, is about the rise and fall of a one-hit band in 1964. It appeared to have the edge with an estimated $6.6 million gross and $3,531 average. "Ducks" scored with $6.55 million and a $3,186 average.

The Hugh Grant medical thriller "Extreme Measures", which opened in the place position last weekend, slipped three notches to fifth with $4.1 million. The 10-day gross for the movie, which is released by Sony Corp's Columbia Pictures, is $13.0 million.

Opening in limited release was the lesbian gangster movie "Bound", which took $904,613 from 262 screens. The movie stars Gina Gershon of "Showgirls" fame and Jennifer Tilly, and is released by Gramercy Pictures, a unit of PolyGram NV.

Reaching the top 10 in its third week of release was "Big Night", the culinary comedy starring Stanley Tucci and Ian Holm. Its $1.2 million weekend gross was good enough for tenth, up from 16th last week. The movie is released by Orion Pictures, a unit of Metromedia International Group Inc.
